column1: # What each agenda platform's own rules say about a program reading it. BUILD_PLAN.md section 6.
# A platform is read by a collector only when its status is `cleared`.
# status   restricted   the vendor's terms or the platform's robots file bar what a collector does
#          candidate    nothing was found against it. Each government's own terms are still unread
#          not_read     the platform's rules have not been read

column3: and the owner has said to go ahead

column2: with what was read and when: docs/sources/tx_agenda_platform_terms.md.

column7: note

The vendor's terms bar automated collection of a government's content for use in any algorithmic or automated decision system without its written consent. Each site's robots file allows the pages, with a 10 second delay.
A CivicPlus product under the same terms. Its robots file allows the pages and reserves rights against training AI models.
A CivicPlus product under the same terms. meetings.municode.com carries the same robots file as CivicClerk.
The robots file on a customer's Granicus host bars every agent but three named search engines.
The robots file on a customer's CivicWeb host bars every agent. The vendor's terms were not read: the robots file settles it.
A customer's Swagit pages are allowed. The host that holds the agenda files answers 403 for its robots file, which the fetcher treats as a refusal.

No robots file on any of the 14 governments' Legistar hosts or on the Legistar Web API, which Granicus publishes for reading public records. Its website terms speak of its own website and say nothing on automated access. The owner said on 2026-11-21 to go ahead. Only the API is read: the hosts that store agenda files bar robots. Each government is read only if its own terms allow it.

No robots file on any of the five county sites or on the association's host for files and calendar feeds. None of the five sites links any terms. The association's terms speak of county.org and its related services. They say nothing on automated access and bar copying for commercial purposes. The software vendor, ezTask, publishes a privacy policy for its own website only. The owner said on 2026-11-22 to start on these sites. The own-sites collector reads them, one county at a time: see config/tx_agenda_site_terms.csv.

There is no vendor. Each government's own robots file and terms decide, one site at a time: see config/tx_agenda_site_terms.csv. Read on 2026-11-21 and 2026-11-22. Of 111 governments, 52 are read. The rest are closed by a robots file, their own terms or a vendor's terms, refused the request, wait on the owner or are not confirmed: docs/sources/tx_agendas_own_sites.md has the count of each. The owner said on 2026-11-21 to build for own sites. The fetcher reads the robots file of every host before every request.

Google's terms, effective July 30, 2026, bar automated access only where it goes against a robots file. The robots files of drive.google.com and docs.google.com allow folder, file and document pages with a 1 second delay and bar the download address. A folder's list is drawn by script, so a collector would need Google's Drive API and a key. Nothing is built. 11 governments.

The robots file of the file host, files.heygov.com, holds no rule. The robots file of the API, api.heygov.com, bars every agent, so the API is never asked. HeyGov's terms speak of its own website, heygov.com, and bar republishing its material. Town Web, which builds the four cities' sites, publishes a privacy policy and no terms. The owner said on 2026-11-22 to go ahead. Sandy Oaks and Shallowater hold their lists as plain links on their own pages and are read. Highland Haven and Sanctuary draw theirs from the API by script and are not. 4 governments, 2 read.

Was AgendaLink. The robots file of the page host and the file host allows every path and says content may not be used to train AI models. No terms of use were found on justmeetings.com, agendalink.app or the meeting page. MCCi links a privacy policy only. 1 government, Cibolo.

The portal's robots address answers with the portal's own page, so it publishes no rules. Laserfiche's terms of use, effective May 22, 2023, say nothing on automated access. 1 government, Sunset Valley, whose own site refused the request for its robots file, so nothing of it is read.

The terms allow personal use only and bar copying any part of the site for commercial, non-profit or public purposes. The robots file allows the document addresses and says content may not be used to train AI models. 2 governments.

No robots file. The terms, version of June 11, 2020, cover the online applications at boardbook.org and bar copying any content by a robot, spider or other automatic process unless the supplier authorizes it. No government is left on it: Milam County also posts on its own site and is read there.

The robots file allows the agenda pages with a 5 second delay. The town site's own terms of service say the license does not include robots or data gathering tools and bar downloading without written consent. 1 government, Trent.
The robots file on towncloud.io bars every agent from every path. The vendor's terms were not read: the robots file settles it. 3 governments.
The robots file on a customer's Diligent Community host bars every agent from every path. The vendor's terms were not read: the robots file settles it. 1 government, Bee Cave.

The robots file on the county's Documents On Demand host bars every agent from every path. The file starts with a byte order mark, which the fetcher strips before reading. The vendor's terms were not read. 1 government, Hood County.

The robots file on www.dropbox.com bars shared file addresses. Dropbox's terms were not read: the robots file settles it. 1 government, De Kalb, whose files could not be told apart as agendas or minutes.

One government is left here: Matagorda County. Its agenda page is on a county association site that is not on a co.<name>.tx.us address. The page showed no agenda on 2026-11-21 and 2026-11-22. The site has no robots file. There is nothing to read. Every other outside service now has its own row.
No Texas government in the inventory uses it. One Michigan government links to it, Hamtramck. Its rules have not been read.
